newsitem.title: USA: IBM introduces new internet server.
newsitem.headline: IBM introduces new internet server.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp on Wednesday introduced a new version of its Net.Commerce merchant server, calling it the first product of its type to use the Secure Electronic Transaction protocol, the industry standard for secure electronic commerce on the Internet's World Wide Web.

IBM said during the Internet Commerce Expo that United Parcel Service of America Inc, Borders Group Inc, Aero-Marine Products and tableware manufacture Hoffmaster had signed on as new customers for the updated server.

The new version of Net.Commerce has several other innovations including a "virtual sales assistant" to guide shoppers to catalog merchandise, technology that allows businesses to use Netscape servers, and new open database support that allows merchants to use any industry database with the new server.
IBM said it would begin shipping the servers on May 30 at a price of $4995.00, the same price as the first release of Net.Commerce last November.
"It's a free upgrade for release one customers who go to release two," said Karl Salnoske, general manager of IBM's internet applications solutions.
